evals.prompt: can you make me a twitter header of mount rainier the way it looks from seattle? something like those engraved line drawings, cream paper, maybe a sun. I'm going to put my profile pic bottom left
evals.expected_output: A 3000x1000 survey-style render of Rainier from a Seattle viewpoint, peak on the right, left third clear, delivered as PNG plus a JPG under 5 MB.
expectations: Looked up Rainier's summit and a Seattle viewpoint instead of guessing coordinates
Ran scripts/render.py with --style survey and --size 3000x1000 (default align right)
Checked the printed peak elevation against the real ~4392 m
Viewed a downscaled preview before delivering
Delivered a JPG under 5 MB alongside or instead of an oversized PNG

evals.prompt: I want a LinkedIn banner of the Grand Tetons as a black woodcut print. Big 'TETONS' title would be cool.
evals.expected_output: A 1584x396 (or 3168x792) woodcut of the Teton Range with a title.
expectations: Used --style woodcut with a LinkedIn banner size (1584x396 or 3168x792)
Passed a --title
Picked a real viewpoint east of the range (e.g. Snake River Overlook or Jenny Lake area)
The range, not a single peak, fills the frame

evals.prompt: Desktop wallpaper please, 4K, Kilimanjaro at night with stars and a moon. centered composition
evals.expected_output: A 3840x2160 nocturne render of Kilimanjaro, centred.
expectations: Used --style nocturne --size 3840x2160 --align center
Looked up Kibo summit coordinates and a viewpoint (e.g. Amboseli)
Moon sits in open sky, not buried behind terrain

evals.prompt: Make a short looping video orbiting the Matterhorn, moonlit line style. I want to post it on Instagram.
evals.expected_output: An MP4 orbit video (nocturne) of the Matterhorn, loopable.
expectations: Used scripts/animate.py with --style nocturne
Used a classic Matterhorn viewpoint such as Riffelsee or Zermatt
Rendered in foreground chunks if the shell has a time limit (--start/--end)
Delivered an MP4 encoded with ffmpeg

evals.prompt: Can you build me one of those interactive pages where I can play with Mount Hood from Portland in different styles and download a header?
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML studio for Mount Hood built with build_studio.py.
expectations: Ran scripts/build_studio.py with --peak, --from, --from-name and --name
Output is a single HTML file under about 1 MB with the DEM embedded
If published as an artifact, declared the downloads capability
Checked the page headless (Playwright) or explained how it was verified

evals.prompt: topographic contour art of the grand canyon from the south rim, I'd like to print it 6000 px wide
evals.expected_output: A canyon render in topo (or a better-suited style with an explanation) at ~6000x2000.
expectations: Targeted a butte or temple inside the canyon and a South Rim viewpoint (e.g. Mather Point)
Rendered at --size 6000x2000
Mentioned honestly if topo reads busy for canyons and offered survey, nocturne or riso

evals.prompt: Show me Denali in every style you have so I can pick one
evals.expected_output: Six Denali renders plus a contact sheet.
expectations: Ran render.py --style all
Produced a contact sheet
Presented the sheet and offered a full-size final of the chosen style

evals.prompt: Everest from Kala Patthar, survey style, label it सगरमाथा with the height
evals.expected_output: An Everest survey render with a Devanagari label that renders correctly (or a clear font fix).
expectations: Used a Kala Patthar viewpoint and Everest summit coordinates
Checked the preview for missing-glyph boxes in the Devanagari label
If glyphs were missing, installed or pointed to a Noto Devanagari font, or told the user plainly
